concepts.why: The patient presented with classic symptoms of appendicitis, including intermittent throbbing abdominal pain that localized to the right lower quadrant, moderate tenderness, and a positive Rovsing sign, along with imaging findings of lobulated tubular soft tissue and inflammation adjacent to the terminal ileum/ileocecal valve.
Biopsy of inflamed areas demonstrated acute inflammation and foci of endometriosis, indicating the presence of endometrial tissue outside the uterus.
Repeat CT showed small-bowel obstruction at the terminal ileum, likely secondary to an adjacent pericecal soft-tissue mass, indicating a mechanical blockage of the small intestine.

The appendix was not identified on imaging, and diagnostic laparoscopy showed no appendix despite full mobilization of the cecum and small-bowel run, raising the possibility of an inverted or retrocecal appendix.

The presence of a pericecal soft-tissue mass and small-bowel obstruction raises the possibility of a neoplastic process, such as a tumor, which could be causing the patient's symptoms and imaging findings.

rationales.F01: Abdominal pain is a non-specific symptom.
rationales.F02: Pain localization to the right lower quadrant is suggestive of appendicitis or inverted appendix.
rationales.F07: Lobulated tubular soft tissue and inflammation adjacent to the terminal ileum/ileocecal valve is highly suggestive of appendicitis or a neoplasm.
rationales.F08: The absence of an identified appendix suggests an inverted appendix or previous appendectomy.
rationales.F09: Mild inflammatory changes and adhesions without an appendix suggest an alternative diagnosis such as endometriosis.
rationales.F10: Biopsy demonstrating acute inflammation and foci of endometriosis strongly supports endometriosis as a diagnosis.
rationales.F12: Small-bowel obstruction at the terminal ileum is highly suggestive of a mechanical obstruction, which could be due to an inverted appendix, neoplasm, or other causes.

frontier_selector.rationale: Biopsy of inflamed areas demonstrated acute inflammation and foci of endometriosis, which explains the patient's symptoms and findings, including the small-bowel obstruction, without strong contradiction.
